newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-RAFTER WINS AS CZECHS SUFFER DOUBLE BLOW.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RAFTER WINS AS CZECHS SUFFER DOUBLE BLOW.

text.p: Pat Rafter gave Australia a 1-0 lead over the Czech Republic in their Davis Cup quarter-final tie on Friday after the Czechs lost a player to illness.
Rafter claimed the opening rubber by beating Martin Damm 6-1 7-6 (9-7) 4-6 6-4 in a tussle lasting two hours and 41 minutes on the grass centre court at Memorial Drive.

The Czechs, already weakened by the absence of four top players, suffered a further setback earlier on Friday when Jiri Novak was forced to withdraw from the second singles rubber against Mark Philippoussis because of a virus.
Rafter, ranked 43 in the world, took advantage of his greater experience on grass to dominate against Damm.
Damm, ranked one place below Rafter, gradually settled into the match but his failure to convert a set point during the second set tie-break eventually proved decisive.
"It's a fantastic feeling to win in a Davis Cup rubber at home. I started really well in the first and second sets but then Martin started putting some more pressure on me," Rafter said afterwards.
Novak, ranked 60, complained of a high temperature on Friday and was ruled out after a medical examination.
"It looks like an influenza virus. He wanted to play but physically he was not able to," Dr Andrew Potter told reporters. "It may take two or three days for him to recover."
The Czech Republic's campaign has been hit by the refusal of Petr Korda, Daniel Vacek, Bohdan Ulihrach and Slava Dosedel to play in the tie.
Novak, who is now ineligible to play in the reverse singles on Sunday, was replaced by Davis Cup debutant David Rikl, ranked a lowly 179.
Philippoussis, who boasts the fastest serve in the world, is ranked 24. He is playing in his first Davis Cup tie on home soil.
Australia upset holders France 4-1 in Sydney in the previous round, while the Czechs defeated India 3-2. The winner of the tie will play either the United States or the Netherlands.
